zero_obligation_gate.rationale: The original task is a finite correction to pinned-state routing after cross-window tab restoration. Native Qt tests prove current-owner state/title for pinned and unpinned tabs, moved-owner API behavior, undo_stack consumption and focused regressions. There is no remaining requested operation. Qt widgets/window registry and fake web tabs are pytest fixtures; no live browser process, remote site connection or authenticated session is evidenced, and those cannot be invented as resource obligations.

evidence.quote: Native undo restored pinned: True tab window: 1 UI title: Pinned old owner index: -1\n
evidence.interpretation: Post-edit production undo routes through tab.set_pinned; the current owner widget receives pinned=True and its actual Qt title is Pinned although the old widget still has no such tab. The authored API tests also move a tab between widgets and verify the inverse pinned state through the current owner.

evidence.quote: Native undo restored pinned: False tab window: 1 UI title: Normal old owner index: -1\n
evidence.interpretation: The independent false case demonstrates restoring an unpinned tab through the new owner with Normal title. Tests assert consumed undo_stack and the expected history.deserialize fixture call in both cases; this is not a live webview history load or remote page fetch.

A separate tool repeats the four owner/API/undo cases with existing pinned/tab-container regressions. Eleven selected native Qt tests pass; the remaining13 were intentionally deselected. The same successful command checks compilation of all four changed Python modules and diff whitespace.
